s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent neurological symptoms with visual disturbances and gastrointestinal symptoms, worsening over time, with associated posterior fossa mass
salient_findings: Intermittent dizziness and blurred vision
Nausea and vomiting that improve after vomiting
Posterior occipital tingling that worsens with emotional agitation
Irregular high-density mass shadow in posterior fossa on CT scan
Irregular mixed signals in medial and posterior cerebellum on MRI
key_facts: 18-year history of intermittent dizziness and blurred vision
Symptoms accompanied by nausea and vomiting
Symptoms improve after vomiting
Posterior occipital tingling worsens with emotional agitation
Symptoms of dizziness and vomiting became more frequent by September 2021
CT scan shows irregular high-density mass shadow in posterior fossa
CT value approximately 93HU
MRI shows irregular mixed signals in medial and posterior cerebellum
Maximum size of the mass: 50mm × 41mm × 51mm
Cyst fluid analysis shows total protein: 15 g/l, albumin: 6.4 g/l, globulin: 8.6 g/l
Cerebrospinal fluid: AFP (negative), β-HCG (negative)

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa mass with cystic components and high-density mass shadow on CT scan

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular mixed signals on MRI and presence of cystic components

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in posterior fossa and presence of cystic components

shortlist.label: Medulloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in posterior fossa and presence of cystic components, although less likely due to patient's age

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of high-density mass shadow on CT scan and possible dural attachment

raw.rationale: The presence of a cystic mass with a mural nodule in the posterior fossa, as shown on MRI, along with the cyst fluid analysis and the patient's symptoms, is most consistent with Hemangioblastoma. The high-density mass shadow on CT and the mixed signals on MRI also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
rejected.why: While pilocytic astrocytoma can present with a cystic component, the location and imaging characteristics are less typical for this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Ependymomas are more commonly associated with the ventricular system and spinal cord, and the imaging findings do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
rejected.why: Medulloblastoma typically presents in the midline of the cerebellum and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging, which does not match the described case

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are usually dural-based and have a different appearance on imaging, with more homogeneous enhancement and a distinct dural tail, which is not described in this case
